title: Game Character Battle
note: The attributes are supplied to the constructors because attack() has no parameters. Use long long arithmetic to avoid overflow for valid int attributes.

title: Smart Parking Fee Calculator
formula: Base fee = hours * rate. Rates: Rs. 10/h and Rs. 30/h. Multiply the entire fee by 0.90 only when hours > 5.
note: Exactly 5 hours has no discount. The same duration is used for both vehicle types so their rates can be compared.

title: File Compression Simulator
prompt: Enter original file size in MB:
formula: Text retains 0.40 * original; image retains 0.70 * original.
note: These percentages are the retained sizes, not the reductions. This simulates sizes; it does not compress an actual file.

title: Food Delivery Time Estimator
note: Convert travel hours into minutes before adding the fixed overhead. Even a zero-distance request includes the stated overhead.

title: Smart Irrigation Controller
note: The allowed moisture range includes 0 and 100. At 100% both systems supply zero litres.

title: Cybersecurity Threat Scanner
formula: Whole-threat convention: remaining = ceil(threats / 10); removed = threats - remaining.
note: The sheet does not specify rounding when 90% is fractional. This solution removes floor(0.9 * threats) whole threats and rounds the remainder up; for 25 it removes 22 and retains 3. For multiples of 10 it removes exactly 90%.

title: Cricket Target Calculator
formula: T20 target = score + ceil(0.01 * score); ODI target = score + ceil(0.02 * score).
note: Round the percentage margin up, then add it to the score. No extra +1 is added: this is the worksheet formula. At score 0 the stated formula gives target 0. Integer arithmetic avoids floating-point rounding errors.

title: Cloud Resource Cost Calculator
formula: Rates: Rs. 5 and Rs. 12 per CPU-hour. If cpuHours > 100, multiply the total by 0.85.
note: Exactly 100 CPU-hours has no discount. Fractional CPU-hours are supported. The discount applies to all usage, not only the hours beyond 100.

title: Robot Navigation System
formula: Time in seconds = distance in metres / speed in m/s. Speeds: 2.0 and 1.2 m/s.
note: The two Robot* pointers point to different derived objects. first->move(distance) and second->move(distance) call their respective overrides. No heap allocation is needed.

title: AI Recommendation Engine
prompt: Enter user rating and popularity (0 to 100):
formula: Personalized: 0.7 * userRating + 0.3 * popularity; trending: 0.3 * userRating + 0.7 * popularity.
note: Both integer inputs must be from 0 through 100. Decimal coefficients preserve fractional scores. Calls use Recommender* pointers as requested.
